name: Ordföljd
subtitle: Word order: verb second, inte and linking words

ruleCards.title: The golden rule: verb second
ruleCards.rule: In a main clause the verb is always in position 2. Position 1, the fundament, can be the subject, a time word, a place word or something else.
examples: I drink coffee in the morning.
In the morning I drink coffee.
ruleCards.watch: Never “Idag jag dricker”: whatever stands in the fundament, the verb comes next.

ruleCards.title: Subject next to the verb
ruleCards.rule: If the subject isn’t in the fundament, it comes straight after the verb. Verb and subject swap places but stay together.

ruleCards.title: Inte and adverbs after the first verb
ruleCards.rule: Inte, alltid, ofta, aldrig and också come right after the first verb. If the subject comes after the verb, they come after the subject.
ruleCards.watch: With a help verb, inte goes between the help verb and the infinitive: Jag vill inte gå.

ruleCards.title: Yes/no questions: verb first
ruleCards.rule: A yes/no question starts with the verb, then the subject. There is no word like English “do”.
ruleCards.watch: With a question word, the question word is the fundament and the verb is still second: Var bor du?

ruleCards.title: Och, men, eller, så, för
ruleCards.rule: These words link two main clauses. They don’t count as the fundament, so the next clause starts as usual with the subject and the verb.
examples: Jag gillar te, men han gillar kaffe.
I like tea, but he likes coffee.
Det regnar, så vi tar bussen.
It’s raining, so we’re taking the bus.
Hon är glad, för hon har semester.
She’s happy, because she’s on holiday.
ruleCards.watch: Så = so (a result). För = because (a reason).

ruleCards.title: Eftersom or på grund av?
ruleCards.rule: Eftersom (because) is followed by a whole clause with a subject and a verb. På grund av (because of) is followed by a noun.
examples: Jag stannar hemma eftersom jag är sjuk.
I’m staying at home because I’m ill.
Tåget är sent på grund av snön.
The train is late because of the snow.
ruleCards.watch: Inside an eftersom clause, inte comes before the verb: eftersom jag inte har tid.

ruleCards.title: Eftersom first: still verb second
ruleCards.rule: If the sentence starts with an eftersom clause, the whole clause is the fundament. The main verb comes next, then the subject.
examples: Eftersom det regnar tar vi bussen.
Because it’s raining, we’re taking the bus.
Eftersom jag är trött går jag hem.
Because I’m tired, I’m going home.
